headline: Oral Poliomyelitis Vaccination Program In Berks County, Pennsylvania
blurb: In a 1963 oral polio vaccine program in Berks County, Pennsylvania, 60.2% of county residents took at least one of the three vaccine types at school and Sunday clinics.

headline: Epidemiologic Notes and Reports A Continuing Measles Outbreak among School-Age Children Despite an Outbreak-Control Program with School Exclusion -- Pennsylvania
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: From September 9 to December 27, 1981, 111 measles cases were reported among school children in Warren County, Pennsylvania, and 146 students without proof of immunity were kept out of school.

headline: 1991: The Philly measles outbreak that killed 9 children
blurb: This 2015 look back describes a Philadelphia measles outbreak that began in October 1990 and in which nine children died, six of them tied to two churches that relied on prayer instead of medical care.

headline: Congenital Rubella Syndrome Among the Amish -- Pennsylvania, 1991-1992
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: A rubella outbreak among the Amish in Pennsylvania ran from February through May 1991, and investigators later identified 11 infants with congenital rubella syndrome.

headline: Hepatitis A Outbreak Associated with Green Onions at a Restaurant --- Monaca, Pennsylvania, 2003
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: As of November 20, 2003, about 555 people had been identified with hepatitis A in an outbreak among patrons of a restaurant in Monaca, Pennsylvania, and three had died.

headline: School Immunizations
blurb: This Pennsylvania Department of Health rule, published on March 4, 2017, replaced the 8-month provisional period for school vaccines with a requirement tied to the first five days of school.

headline: Health Department Update on Measles Outbreak – January 18
source: City of Philadelphia, Department of Public Health
blurb: Philadelphia's health department reported a total of nine confirmed measles cases in an outbreak in the city, eight of them counted as Philadelphia cases.
